headline: Pope Leo called AI an 'instrument of domination, exclusion and death.' Anthropic was in the room
liCaption:
The Vatican just issued a historic rebuke of artificial intelligence that should alarm every technology leader, investor, and strategist paying attention to the AI industry's future.

Pope Leo XIV's latest encyclical explicitly condemned AI as an 'instrument of domination, exclusion and death,' marking the first time the Catholic Church has taken such a direct stance on the technology. Most significantly, Anthropic—one of the world's leading AI safety companies—was present during these discussions, signaling that the moral and ethical reckoning with AI is no longer a fringe concern but a central conversation involving the industry's key players.

This moment reflects a critical inflection point in how AI companies are being perceived and held accountable. We're witnessing a shift from techno-optimism to institutional scrutiny. When the Church engages directly with AI developers, it signals that traditional power structures—religious, political, and social—are taking existential risks seriously. For Anthropic and competitors like OpenAI, this represents both a challenge and an opportunity to demonstrate meaningful alignment with broader human values.

The broader AI industry should view this as a wake-up call. Regulatory frameworks are coming regardless, but the Church's intervention suggests that moral legitimacy—not just technical capability—will determine which AI companies thrive long-term. Companies ignoring ethical frameworks risk becoming pariahs, while those embracing transparency and accountability could gain significant competitive advantages.

Looking forward, expect more institutional actors—governments, religious organizations, academic bodies—to demand seats at the table where AI futures are decided. The companies that proactively engage with these stakeholders will shape the narrative; those that resist will find themselves in reactive, defensive positions.

The era of moving fast and breaking things in AI is definitively over. What comes next belongs to those who can move thoughtfully and build trust.

Source: Fortune · https://fortune.com/2026/05/25/pope-leo-xiv-ai-domination-death-anthropic-olah-encyclical/
